/-!
# Finite-morphism embeddings

This file supplies two pieces of the standard proof that finite morphisms are
projective. Over an affine target, a finite morphism is a closed subscheme of
finite-dimensional affine space. At the other end of the compactification
argument, a proper immersion into projective space is already closed.

The remaining geometric step is to place the affine embedding in a projective
chart and globalize it over the target. These results isolate both sides of
that step without adding a projectivity hypothesis.
-/

open CategoryTheory Limits MvPolynomial

noncomputable section

universe u

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

namespace Scheme.Hom.IsProjective

variable {X S : Scheme.{u}} {pi : X ⟶ S}

/-- A proper morphism that factors through projective space by an immersion is
projective. Properness makes the immersion closed. -/
theorem of_isProper_of_immersion (hpi : IsProper pi) {n : Type u} [Finite n]
    (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)) (hi : IsImmersion i)
    (hcomp : i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi) : pi.IsProjective := by
  letI : IsImmersion i := hi
  haveI : IsProper (i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S)) := hcomp ▸ hpi
  haveI : IsProper i := IsProper.of_comp i (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S)
  haveI : IsClosedImmersion i :=
    (IsClosedImmersion.iff_isProper_and_mono (f := i)).mpr
      ⟨inferInstance, inferInstance⟩
  exact ⟨n, inferInstance, i, inferInstance, hcomp⟩

/-- An algebra-generating family makes the corresponding morphism from an
affine spectrum to polynomial affine space a closed immersion. This is the
ring-level form of the chosen-generator embedding criterion. -/
theorem isClosedImmersion_SpecMap_aeval_of_adjoin_eq_top
    {R A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    {n : Type u} (a : n → A)
    (hgen : Algebra.adjoin R (Set.range a) = ⊤) :
    IsClosedImmersion (Spec.map
      (CommRingCat.ofHom (MvPolynomial.aeval (R := R) a).toRingHom)) := by
  apply IsClosedImmersion.spec_of_surjective
  change Function.Surjective (MvPolynomial.aeval (R := R) a)
  rw [← AlgHom.range_eq_top, ← Algebra.adjoin_range_eq_range_aeval]

/-- A specified finite module-spanning family in the affine source ring
defines a closed immersion into affine space over the base. This is the
chosen-generator form of `exists_closedImmersion_affineSpace`, used when the
generators on two base charts have already been aligned. -/
theorem isClosedImmersion_homOfVector_of_span_eq_top
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffine X] [IsAffine Y]
    {n : Type u} [Finite n] (a : n → Γ(X, ⊤))
    (hspan :
      letI : Algebra Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤) := RingHom.toAlgebra f.appTop.hom
      Submodule.span Γ(Y, ⊤) (Set.range a) = ⊤) :
    IsClosedImmersion (AffineSpace.homOfVector f a) := by
  classical
  letI : Fintype n := Fintype.ofFinite n
  letI : Algebra Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤) := RingHom.toAlgebra f.appTop.hom
  let i : X ⟶ 𝔸(n; Y) := AffineSpace.homOfVector f a
  have hsurj : Function.Surjective (Fintype.linearCombination Γ(Y, ⊤) a) := by
    rw [← LinearMap.range_eq_top, Fintype.range_linearCombination, hspan]
  apply IsClosedImmersion.of_surjective_of_isAffine
  intro x
  obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := hsurj x
  let p : MvPolynomial n Γ(Y, ⊤) :=
    ∑ j, C (c j) * MvPolynomial.X j
  refine ⟨(AffineSpace.isoOfIsAffine n Y).hom.appTop
    ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of (MvPolynomial n Γ(Y, ⊤)))).inv p), ?_⟩
  rw [AffineSpace.isoOfIsAffine_hom_appTop]
  simp only [CommRingCat.comp_apply, Iso.inv_hom_id_apply]
  change (i.appTop.hom.comp
    (eval₂Hom (𝔸(n; Y) ↘ Y).appTop.hom (AffineSpace.coord Y))) p =
      Fintype.linearCombination Γ(Y, ⊤) a c
  have heval :
      i.appTop.hom.comp
        (eval₂Hom (𝔸(n; Y) ↘ Y).appTop.hom (AffineSpace.coord Y)) =
        eval₂Hom f.appTop.hom a := by
    apply MvPolynomial.ringHom_ext
    · intro r
      simp only [RingHom.comp_apply, eval₂Hom_C]
      have h := congrArg Scheme.Hom.appTop
        (AffineSpace.homOfVector_over f a)
      rw [Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop] at h
      exact congrArg (fun e : Γ(Y, ⊤) ⟶ Γ(X, ⊤) => e.hom r) h
    · intro j
      simp [i]
  rw [heval, Fintype.linearCombination_apply]
  simp only [p, map_sum, map_mul, coe_eval₂Hom, eval₂_C, eval₂_X,
    Algebra.smul_def]
  change (∑ x, f.appTop.hom (c x) * a x) =
    ∑ x, f.appTop.hom (c x) * a x
  rfl

/-!
# The projective immersion attached to a finite two-chart map

The two distinguished homogeneous coordinates cut out target charts whose
inverse images are exactly the two pulled-back Laurent charts.  On each chart,
the global relative coordinate morphism is the closed immersion supplied by
the algebra-generating coordinate family.  Target-locality then makes the
global morphism an immersion.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

  TopologicalSpace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
variable {Y C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
variable {D : LaurentChartData Y} {pi : C ⟶ Y}
variable (G : D.FiniteMapGenerators pi)

/-- The coordinate normalized to one on the first source chart. -/
abbrev firstIndex : G.ProjectiveIndex :=
  Sum.inl ⟨0, Nat.zero_lt_succ G.d⟩

/-- The coordinate normalized to one on the second source chart. -/
abbrev secondIndex : G.ProjectiveIndex :=
  Sum.inl ⟨G.d, Nat.lt_succ_self G.d⟩

/-- The target chart selected by the first distinguished coordinate. -/
def targetOpen0 : (ℙ(G.ProjectiveIndex; Spec (.of k))).Opens :=
  ProjectiveSpace.toProjInt G.ProjectiveIndex (Spec (.of k)) ⁻¹ᵁ
    Proj.basicOpen
      (homogeneousSubmodule G.ProjectiveIndex (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X G.firstIndex)

/-- The target chart selected by the second distinguished coordinate. -/
def targetOpen1 : (ℙ(G.ProjectiveIndex; Spec (.of k))).Opens :=
  ProjectiveSpace.toProjInt G.ProjectiveIndex (Spec (.of k)) ⁻¹ᵁ
    Proj.basicOpen
      (homogeneousSubmodule G.ProjectiveIndex (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X G.secondIndex)

/-- The first target open is the corresponding relative affine chart. -/
def targetOpen0IsoAffineChartAt :
    G.targetOpen0.toScheme ≅
      ProjectiveSpace.affineChartAt G.ProjectiveIndex G.firstIndex (Spec (.of k)) := by
  apply IsOpenImmersion.isoOfRangeEq G.targetOpen0.ι
    (ProjectiveSpace.affineChartAt.incl
      G.ProjectiveIndex G.firstIndex (Spec (.of k)))
  rw [Scheme.Opens.range_ι, ← Scheme.Hom.coe_opensRange,
    ProjectiveSpace.affineChartAt.opensRange_incl, targetOpen0]

/-- The second target open is the corresponding relative affine chart. -/
def targetOpen1IsoAffineChartAt :
    G.targetOpen1.toScheme ≅
      ProjectiveSpace.affineChartAt G.ProjectiveIndex G.secondIndex (Spec (.of k)) := by
  apply IsOpenImmersion.isoOfRangeEq G.targetOpen1.ι
    (ProjectiveSpace.affineChartAt.incl
      G.ProjectiveIndex G.secondIndex (Spec (.of k)))
  rw [Scheme.Opens.range_ι, ← Scheme.Hom.coe_opensRange,
    ProjectiveSpace.affineChartAt.opensRange_incl, targetOpen1]

@[reassoc]
theorem targetOpen0IsoAffineChartAt_hom_incl :
    G.targetOpen0IsoAffineChartAt.hom ≫
        ProjectiveSpace.affineChartAt.incl
          G.ProjectiveIndex G.firstIndex (Spec (.of k)) =
      G.targetOpen0.ι :=
  IsOpenImmersion.isoOfRangeEq_hom_fac _ _ _

@[reassoc]
theorem targetOpen1IsoAffineChartAt_hom_incl :
    G.targetOpen1IsoAffineChartAt.hom ≫
        ProjectiveSpace.affineChartAt.incl
          G.ProjectiveIndex G.secondIndex (Spec (.of k)) =
      G.targetOpen1.ι :=
  IsOpenImmersion.isoOfRangeEq_hom_fac _ _ _

/-- Removing the normalized coordinate does not change algebra generation on
the first chart. -/
theorem adjoin_projectiveCoordinates0_ne :
    Algebra.adjoin k
      (Set.range fun j : {j : G.ProjectiveIndex // j ≠ G.firstIndex} ↦
        G.projectiveCoordinates0 j.1) = ⊤ := by
  have hfull := G.adjoin_chart0 D pi
  apply top_unique
  rw [← hfull]
  apply Algebra.adjoin_le
  rintro z ⟨j, rfl⟩
  by_cases hj : j = G.firstIndex
  · subst j
    change G.projectiveCoordinates0 G.firstIndex ∈ _
    rw [G.projectiveCoordinates0_zero]
    exact Subalgebra.one_mem _
  · exact Algebra.subset_adjoin ⟨⟨j, hj⟩, rfl⟩

/-- Removing the normalized coordinate does not change algebra generation on
the second chart. -/
theorem adjoin_projectiveCoordinates1_ne :
    Algebra.adjoin k
      (Set.range fun j : {j : G.ProjectiveIndex // j ≠ G.secondIndex} ↦
        G.projectiveCoordinates1 j.1) = ⊤ := by
  have hfull := G.adjoin_chart1 D pi
  apply top_unique
  rw [← hfull]
  apply Algebra.adjoin_le
  rintro z ⟨j, rfl⟩
  by_cases hj : j = G.secondIndex
  · subst j
    change G.projectiveCoordinates1 G.secondIndex ∈ _
    rw [G.projectiveCoordinates1_last]
    exact Subalgebra.one_mem _
  · exact Algebra.subset_adjoin ⟨⟨j, hj⟩, rfl⟩

/-- The section ring of an open and the global sections of its open subscheme
are canonically isomorphic. -/
def openSectionsEquiv (U : C.left.Opens) :
    Γ(C.left, U) ≃+* Γ(U.toScheme, ⊤) :=
  (asIso (U.ι.appLE U ⊤ U.ι_preimage_self.ge)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv

/-- The section-ring equivalence respects the structural `k`-algebra map. -/
theorem openSectionsEquiv_algebraMap (U : C.left.Opens) (c : k) :
    openSectionsEquiv U (algebraMap k Γ(C.left, U) c) =
      (U.ι ≫ C.hom).appTop.hom
        ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv.hom c) := by
  change (U.ι.appLE U ⊤ U.ι_preimage_self.ge).hom
      (algebraMap k Γ(C.left, U) c) = _
  have hL : algebraMap k Γ(C.left, U) c =
      (C.left.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : U ≤ ⊤)).op).hom
        (C.hom.appTop.hom ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv.hom c)) := rfl
  rw [hL]
  change (C.left.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : U ≤ ⊤)).op ≫
      U.ι.appLE U ⊤ U.ι_preimage_self.ge).hom
        (C.hom.appTop.hom ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv.hom c)) = _
  rw [Scheme.Hom.map_appLE, Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop]
  simp only [Scheme.Hom.appLE, Scheme.Hom.preimage_top, homOfLE_refl,
    op_id, CommRingCat.comp_apply]
  have hid := congrArg
    (fun q : Γ(U.toScheme, ⊤) ⟶ Γ(U.toScheme, ⊤) ↦ q.hom
      (U.ι.appTop.hom (C.hom.appTop.hom
        ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv.hom c))))
    (U.toScheme.presheaf.map_id (Opposite.op (⊤ : U.toScheme.Opens)))
  simpa using hid

/-- The section-ring equivalence is the inverse of the canonical top-sections
isomorphism used in `Opens.toSpecΓ`. -/
theorem topIso_inv_eq_appLE (U : C.left.Opens) :
    U.topIso.inv = U.ι.appLE U ⊤ U.ι_preimage_self.ge := by
  rw [Scheme.Opens.topIso_inv, Scheme.Opens.ι_appLE]
  rfl

/-- The affine spectrum structural map defined by the canonical section-ring
algebra is the structural map of the open subscheme. -/
theorem toSpecΓ_specToBase (U : C.left.Opens) :
    U.toSpecΓ ≫
        ProjectiveSpace.Coordinates.specToBase
          (k := k) (B := Γ(C.left, U)) =
      U.ι ≫ C.hom := by
  apply ext_to_Spec
  ext c
  change (U.toSpecΓ ≫
      ProjectiveSpace.Coordinates.specToBase
        (k := k) (B := Γ(C.left, U))).appTop.hom
          ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv.hom c) =
    (U.ι ≫ C.hom).appTop.hom
      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv.hom c)
  rw [Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop]
  change U.toSpecΓ.appTop.hom
      ((ProjectiveSpace.Coordinates.specToBase
        (k := k) (B := Γ(C.left, U))).appTop.hom
          ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv.hom c)) = _
  have hbase :
      (ProjectiveSpace.Coordinates.specToBase
        (k := k) (B := Γ(C.left, U))).appTop.hom
          ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv.hom c) =
        (Scheme.ΓSpecIso Γ(C.left, U)).inv.hom
          (algebraMap k Γ(C.left, U) c) := by
    rw [ProjectiveSpace.Coordinates.specToBase,
      ← CommRingCat.comp_apply, ← Scheme.ΓSpecIso_inv_naturality,
      CommRingCat.comp_apply, ConcreteCategory.hom_ofHom]
    rw [Scheme.ΓSpecIso_inv, Scheme.ΓSpecIso_inv]
  rw [hbase, Scheme.Opens.toSpecΓ_appTop]
  rw [topIso_inv_eq_appLE U]
  simp only [CommRingCat.comp_apply, Iso.inv_hom_id_apply]
  change openSectionsEquiv U (algebraMap k Γ(C.left, U) c) = _
  exact openSectionsEquiv_algebraMap U c

/-- The factor of the global coordinate morphism through the first relative

def chartFactor0 :

  (pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₁).toSpecΓ ≫
    ProjectiveSpace.Coordinates.toAffineChartAt G.secondIndex

@[reassoc]

-- The target-local proof elaborates through two nested pullback presentations.
/-- A proper source carrying a finite two-chart map is projective over the
base field. -/
theorem isProjective [IsFinite pi.left] [IsProper C.hom] :
    C.hom.IsProjective := by
  exact Scheme.Hom.IsProjective.of_isProper_of_immersion
    (pi := C.hom) (by infer_instance) G.toProjectiveSpace
      G.isImmersion_toProjectiveSpace G.toProjectiveSpace_over

theorem isProjective_of_finiteMap
    (D : LaurentChartData Y) (pi : C ⟶ Y)
    [IsFinite pi.left] [IsProper C.hom] : C.hom.IsProjective := by
  obtain ⟨G⟩ := D.nonempty_finiteMapGenerators pi
  exact G.isProjective

/-!
# Demand ledger for projective-morphism infrastructure

This file records the projective infrastructure demanded by the Picard
representability seam.  It is a ledger, not a second projectivity API.

## A seam-facing sufficient producer

`Scheme.PointedPicSharpRep` asks for a representing scheme that is locally of
finite type and satisfies `Scheme.FiniteInAffine`.  It does not ask for a line
bundle.  The existing project-local route supplies those two side conditions
from a coproduct of H-quasi-projective pieces:

* `Scheme.Hom.IsHQuasiProjective` is the universe-polymorphic embedding
  predicate from `Picard/ProjectiveMorphismBasic.lean`;
* `Scheme.locallyOfFiniteType_sigma` and
  `Scheme.finiteInAffine_over_sigma_of_isHQuasiProjective` aggregate the two
  side conditions in `Picard/QuasiProjectiveFiniteInAffine.lean`;
* at `Scheme.{0}`, `Scheme.Hom.IsHQuasiProjective.exists_isHQuasiProjectiveWith`
  adds a carried pullback of `O(1)`.  Thus the existing
  `IsHQuasiProjectiveWith` is already the required very-ample output; defining
  an alias named `IsVeryAmple` would only re-spell it.

A strong sufficient producer is recorded as
`pointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces_demand`: if proved, it would construct the
representing coproduct and prove H-quasi-projectivity piecewise.  It is not the
minimal seam price: `HasGoodGaloisLevel` and `seamClauseOne` expose a weaker
single-finite-Galois-level route.  The two proved adapters below are only typing
and consumption checks.  They both assume `H`, whose closed proposition
packages the representation witness; they produce no representation and do not
reduce the current seam debt.  Their signatures add no explicit
`RepresentableBy` argument.

## The D4' Grassmannian demand

The committed divisor route has one narrower projective consumer before the
Picard-piece producer exists.  D3' must carve a scheme `Z` with a quasi-compact
immersion into the chosen scheme representing a Grassmannian over a field.  D4'
then needs `Z` to be H-quasi-projective so that its finite point sets lie in
affine opens.  The existing `IsHQuasiProjective.comp_isImmersion` performs the
last step. The field representer is now supplied directly by
`Scheme.Grassmannian.representingScheme_isHQuasiProjective_of_field`.

`Projective/Grassmannian.lean` proves the field-specialised transport: it derives
global freeness on `Spec K`, base-changes the absolute Grassmannian, and uses
uniqueness of representing objects. `Projective/GrassmannianProjective.lean`
now supplies the absolute certificate by the Plucker embedding. Properness of
the absolute Grassmannian is combined there with the proved immersion into
relative projective space; properness alone would not imply the project-local
definition of H-quasi-projectivity.

## No current section-Proj demand

Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.Proj` is the Proj of an `N`-graded commutative
ring, not a relative Proj of a sheaf of graded algebras.  The project has enough
section-ring data to make that absolute Proj elaborate after two elementary
structure assemblies, but no Picard declaration consumes it: there is no
intrinsic `picSharpDeg` carrier, representing scheme for such a component, or
Picard-piece line bundle from which to form the section ring.  Consequently
those assemblies are not demands of the seam and are deliberately absent from
this ledger.

The live predecessor is the intrinsic degree and representation construction;
only that construction can expose a narrower Proj or ampleness signature.  A
general relative-Proj gluing theory or a general ample predicate must not be
built before then.  The whole Picard scheme must also not be strengthened to
`IsProjective`: its degree-graded coproduct is not quasi-compact, as recorded by
`Picard/AmbientPicNotProper.lean` and `Scheme.PointedPicSharpRepProjective`.

## Existing inputs

Curve projectivity is already produced by
`Adelic.isProjective_of_smoothProperGeometricallyIntegral`.  The carried
`O(1)`, base-change and open-image transport, `FiniteInAffine` transport, and
Over-coproduct assembly remain owned by the established Picard modules and are
imported here read-only.
-/

noncomputable section

universe u

namespace AlgebraicGeometry
namespace Scheme

/-- A sufficient projective presentation that the pointed Picard reduction can
consume at every universe: `picSharp` is represented by a coproduct of
H-quasi-projective schemes over the ground field.

The integer index records the intended degree pieces without introducing a
second, currently nonexistent `picSharpDeg` functor.  This closed proposition
contains the representation witness in its conclusion; no downstream theorem
takes an explicit representation-witness argument.  This keeps the strict
binder count unchanged, but it remains logically a representation assumption. -/
def PointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces : Prop :=
  ∀ {K : Type u} [Field K] (E : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))),
    ∀ [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 E.hom] [IsProper E.hom]
      [GeometricallyIntegral E.hom],
      HasRationalPoint E →
        ∃ X : ℤ → Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)),
          Nonempty ((PicScheme.picSharp E).RepresentableBy (∐ X)) ∧
            ∀ d, (X d).hom.IsHQuasiProjective

/-- A piecewise H-quasi-projective representation supplies exactly the local
finite type and `FiniteInAffine` conjuncts of `PointedPicSharpRep`.

This is the seam-side typecheck for the ledger, not producer movement. -/
theorem pointedPicSharpRep_of_quasiProjectivePieces
    (H : PointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces.{u}) :
    PointedPicSharpRep.{u} := by
  intro K _ E _ _ _ hpt
  obtain ⟨X, hrep, hX⟩ := H E hpt
  refine ⟨∐ X, hrep, ?_, ?_⟩
  · exact locallyOfFiniteType_sigma X fun d => (hX d).locallyOfFiniteType
  · exact finiteInAffine_over_sigma_of_isHQuasiProjective X hX

/-- Conditional on the open ledger demand, the central seam follows verbatim,
with no rational point binder on the target theorem.  This adapter is not a
sorry-free producer or a discharge of the seam. -/
theorem fgaPicardRepresentability_of_quasiProjectivePieces
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
    (H : PointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces.{u}) :
    (∃ X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)),
        Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
          LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom) ∧
      (HasRationalPoint C → IsIso (PicScheme.picEtComparison C)) :=
  fgaPicardRepresentability_of_pointedPicSharpRep C
    (pointedPicSharpRep_of_quasiProjectivePieces H)

/-- **Open sufficient producer.** Construct the pointed Picard representer as a
coproduct of H-quasi-projective pieces.  This is deliberately stronger than the
single-finite-Galois-level price of seam clause one. -/
theorem pointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces_demand :
    PointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces.{u} := by
  sorry

end Scheme

namespace Scheme
namespace Grassmannian

/-- A quasi-compact D3' immersion into an H-quasi-projective Grassmannian gives
the exact H-quasi-projectivity certificate carried by D4'.

This is a typing check for the demand above, not a construction of the missing
D3' locus or of the ambient Grassmannian certificate. -/
theorem d4Locus_isHQuasiProjective_over
    {S : Scheme.{0}} [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    {V : S.Modules} {r d : ℕ}
    (hV : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank V r)
    (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdr : d ≤ r)
    (Z : Over S)
    (j : Z ⟶ representingScheme hV hd hdr)
    [IsImmersion j.left] [QuasiCompact j.left]
    (hGr : (representingScheme hV hd hdr).hom.IsHQuasiProjective) :
    Z.hom.IsHQuasiProjective := by
  rw [← j.w]
  exact hGr.comp_isImmersion j.left

end Grassmannian
end Scheme
end AlgebraicGeometry

body: 'AJC projective-morphism demand ledger landed (phase 0)


  Commit 1b7d1ff7b6 adds AlgebraicJacobian/Projective/DemandLedger.lean. The exact
  seam-facing proposition is Scheme.PointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces: for every
  pointed smooth proper geometrically integral curve, picSharp is represented by an
  integer-indexed coproduct of H-quasi-projective pieces. Proved adapters consume
  it into PointedPicSharpRep and then the verbatim fgaPicardRepresentability conclusion;
  neither adapter takes an explicit representation-witness argument.


  The sole open seam producer is pointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces_demand. Existing
  CurveProjectivity, IsHQuasiProjective, Scheme.{0} IsHQuasiProjectiveWith carried
  O(1), FiniteInAffine transport/aggregation, and Over coproduct assembly are inventory,
  not duplicated APIs. At Scheme.{0}, the carried certificate is already the faithful
  very-ample output; no IsVeryAmple alias is introduced.


  The only conditional Proj demands currently justified are sectionGradedRing_gcommRing_demand
  and sectionGradedRing_gradedRing_demand, needed before mathlib Proj can consume
  the existing section direct sum. No general relative-Proj gluing or ample predicate
  is authorized until a narrower Picard consumer elaborates. In particular, ampleness
  must not be defined tautologically as a very-ample power, and the whole degree-graded
  Picard coproduct must not be strengthened to projective.


  Ownership boundary with ajc-kleiman-rewire was agreed and archived in I-1822. Roadmap:
  AJC.picrep.projective-infra and children.'

     9	/-!
    10	# Demand ledger for projective-morphism infrastructure
    11	
    12	This file records the projective infrastructure demanded by the Picard
    13	representability seam.  It is a ledger, not a second projectivity API.
    14	
    15	## A seam-facing sufficient producer
    16	
    17	`Scheme.PointedPicSharpRep` asks for a representing scheme that is locally of
    18	finite type and satisfies `Scheme.FiniteInAffine`.  It does not ask for a line
    19	bundle.  The existing project-local route supplies those two side conditions
    20	from a coproduct of H-quasi-projective pieces:
    21	
    22	* `Scheme.Hom.IsHQuasiProjective` is the universe-polymorphic embedding
    23	  predicate from `Picard/ProjectiveMorphismBasic.lean`;
    24	* `Scheme.locallyOfFiniteType_sigma` and
    25	  `Scheme.finiteInAffine_over_sigma_of_isHQuasiProjective` aggregate the two
    26	  side conditions in `Picard/QuasiProjectiveFiniteInAffine.lean`;
    27	* at `Scheme.{0}`, `Scheme.Hom.IsHQuasiProjective.exists_isHQuasiProjectiveWith`
    28	  adds a carried pullback of `O(1)`.  Thus the existing
    29	  `IsHQuasiProjectiveWith` is already the required very-ample output; defining
    30	  an alias named `IsVeryAmple` would only re-spell it.
    31	
    32	A strong sufficient producer is recorded as
    33	`pointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces_demand`: if proved, it would construct the
    34	representing coproduct and prove H-quasi-projectivity piecewise.  It is not the
    35	minimal seam price: `HasGoodGaloisLevel` and `seamClauseOne` expose a weaker
    36	single-finite-Galois-level route.  The two proved adapters below are only typing
    37	and consumption checks.  They both assume `H`, whose closed proposition
    38	packages the representation witness; they produce no representation and do not
    39	reduce the current seam debt.  Their signatures add no explicit
    40	`RepresentableBy` argument.
    41	
    42	## The D4' Grassmannian demand
    43	
    44	The committed divisor route has one narrower projective consumer before the
    45	Picard-piece producer exists.  D3' must carve a scheme `Z` with a quasi-compact
    46	immersion into the chosen scheme representing a Grassmannian over a field.  D4'
    47	then needs `Z` to be H-quasi-projective so that its finite point sets lie in
    48	affine opens.  The existing `IsHQuasiProjective.comp_isImmersion` performs the
    49	last step. The field representer is now supplied directly by
    50	`Scheme.Grassmannian.representingScheme_isHQuasiProjective_of_field`.
    51	
    52	`Projective/Grassmannian.lean` proves the field-specialised transport: it derives
    53	global freeness on `Spec K`, base-changes the absolute Grassmannian, and uses
    54	uniqueness of representing objects. `Projective/GrassmannianProjective.lean`
    55	now supplies the absolute certificate by the Plucker embedding. Properness of
    56	the absolute Grassmannian is combined there with the proved immersion into
    57	relative projective space; properness alone would not imply the project-local
    58	definition of H-quasi-projectivity.
    59	
    60	## No current section-Proj demand
    61	
    62	Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.Proj` is the Proj of an `N`-graded commutative
    63	ring, not a relative Proj of a sheaf of graded algebras.  The project has enough
    64	section-ring data to make that absolute Proj elaborate after two elementary
    65	structure assemblies, but no Picard declaration consumes it: there is no
    66	intrinsic `picSharpDeg` carrier, representing scheme for such a component, or
    67	Picard-piece line bundle from which to form the section ring.  Consequently
    68	those assemblies are not demands of the seam and are deliberately absent from
    69	this ledger.
    70	
    71	The live predecessor is the intrinsic degree and representation construction;
    72	only that construction can expose a narrower Proj or ampleness signature.  A
    73	general relative-Proj gluing theory or a general ample predicate must not be
    74	built before then.  The whole Picard scheme must also not be strengthened to
    75	`IsProjective`: its degree-graded coproduct is not quasi-compact, as recorded by
    76	`Picard/AmbientPicNotProper.lean` and `Scheme.PointedPicSharpRepProjective`.
    77	
    78	## Existing inputs
    79	
    80	Curve projectivity is already produced by
    81	`Adelic.isProjective_of_smoothProperGeometricallyIntegral`.  The carried
    82	`O(1)`, base-change and open-image transport, `FiniteInAffine` transport, and
    83	Over-coproduct assembly remain owned by the established Picard modules and are
    84	imported here read-only.
    85	-/

    96	/-- A sufficient projective presentation that the pointed Picard reduction can
    97	consume at every universe: `picSharp` is represented by a coproduct of
    98	H-quasi-projective schemes over the ground field.
    99	
   100	The integer index records the intended degree pieces without introducing a
   101	second, currently nonexistent `picSharpDeg` functor.  This closed proposition
   102	contains the representation witness in its conclusion; no downstream theorem
   103	takes an explicit representation-witness argument.  This keeps the strict
   104	binder count unchanged, but it remains logically a representation assumption. -/
   105	def PointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces : Prop :=
   106	  ∀ {K : Type u} [Field K] (E : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))),
   107	    ∀ [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 E.hom] [IsProper E.hom]
   108	      [GeometricallyIntegral E.hom],
   109	      HasRationalPoint E →
   110	        ∃ X : ℤ → Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)),
   111	          Nonempty ((PicScheme.picSharp E).RepresentableBy (∐ X)) ∧
   112	            ∀ d, (X d).hom.IsHQuasiProjective
   113	
   114	/-- A piecewise H-quasi-projective representation supplies exactly the local
   115	finite type and `FiniteInAffine` conjuncts of `PointedPicSharpRep`.
   116	
   117	This is the seam-side typecheck for the ledger, not producer movement. -/
   118	theorem pointedPicSharpRep_of_quasiProjectivePieces
   119	    (H : PointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces.{u}) :
   120	    PointedPicSharpRep.{u} := by
   121	  intro K _ E _ _ _ hpt
   122	  obtain ⟨X, hrep, hX⟩ := H E hpt
   123	  refine ⟨∐ X, hrep, ?_, ?_⟩
   124	  · exact locallyOfFiniteType_sigma X fun d => (hX d).locallyOfFiniteType
   125	  · exact finiteInAffine_over_sigma_of_isHQuasiProjective X hX
   126	
   127	/-- Conditional on the open ledger demand, the central seam follows verbatim,
   128	with no rational point binder on the target theorem.  This adapter is not a
   129	sorry-free producer or a discharge of the seam. -/
   130	theorem fgaPicardRepresentability_of_quasiProjectivePieces
   131	    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   132	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   133	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
   134	    (H : PointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces.{u}) :
   135	    (∃ X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)),
   136	        Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
   137	          LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom) ∧
   138	      (HasRationalPoint C → IsIso (PicScheme.picEtComparison C)) :=
   139	  fgaPicardRepresentability_of_pointedPicSharpRep C
   140	    (pointedPicSharpRep_of_quasiProjectivePieces H)
   141	
   142	/-- **Open sufficient producer.** Construct the pointed Picard representer as a
   143	coproduct of H-quasi-projective pieces.  This is deliberately stronger than the
   144	single-finite-Galois-level price of seam clause one. -/
   145	theorem pointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces_demand :
   146	    PointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces.{u} := by
   147	  sorry

   154	/-- A quasi-compact D3' immersion into an H-quasi-projective Grassmannian gives
   155	the exact H-quasi-projectivity certificate carried by D4'.
   156	
   157	This is a typing check for the demand above, not a construction of the missing
   158	D3' locus or of the ambient Grassmannian certificate. -/
   159	theorem d4Locus_isHQuasiProjective_over
   160	    {S : Scheme.{0}} [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
   161	    {V : S.Modules} {r d : ℕ}
   162	    (hV : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank V r)
   163	    (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdr : d ≤ r)
   164	    (Z : Over S)
   165	    (j : Z ⟶ representingScheme hV hd hdr)
   166	    [IsImmersion j.left] [QuasiCompact j.left]
   167	    (hGr : (representingScheme hV hd hdr).hom.IsHQuasiProjective) :
   168	    Z.hom.IsHQuasiProjective := by
   169	  rw [← j.w]
   170	  exact hGr.comp_isImmersion j.left

    11	/-!
    12	# The universal locally closed rank locus
    13	
    14	This file upgrades the matrix-defined flattening stratum from flatness to the
    15	rank-indexed local-freeness predicate used by the Grassmannian construction.
    16	In rank one it is therefore the universal locally closed locus on which the
    17	module becomes an invertible sheaf.
    18	
    19	The construction is unconditional.  It uses the existing presentation charts
    20	and their entry-ideal strata; it does not assume Picard representability or a
    21	rational point.
    22	-/

    38	/-- An explicit rank-`e` basis of sections on an affine open trivialises the
    39	corresponding restriction of a quasi-coherent module. -/
    40	theorem pullback_isFreeOfRank_of_sectionsEquiv
    41	    (M : X.Modules) [M.IsQuasicoherent] {U : X.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
    42	    (e : ℕ) (E : (Fin e → Γ(X, U)) ≃ₗ[Γ(X, U)] Γ(M, U)) :
    43	    Nonempty ((pullback U.ι).obj M ≅
    44	      SheafOfModules.free (R := U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin e))) := by
    45	  let N := (pullback hU.fromSpec).obj M
    46	  haveI : N.IsQuasicoherent := pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom hU.fromSpec M inferInstance
    47	  haveI : IsIso (fromSpecRestrictTopHom M hU) :=
    48	    fromSpecRestrictTopHom_isIso M hU
    49	  haveI : IsIso ((restrictFunctorIsoPullback hU.fromSpec).hom.app M) := inferInstance
    50	  haveI : IsIso
    51	      (moduleSpecΓFunctor.map ((restrictFunctorIsoPullback hU.fromSpec).hom.app M)) :=
    52	    inferInstance
    53	  let sectionHom : ModuleCat.of Γ(X, U) Γ(M, U) ⟶ moduleSpecΓFunctor.obj N :=
    54	    fromSpecRestrictTopHom M hU ≫
    55	      moduleSpecΓFunctor.map ((restrictFunctorIsoPullback hU.fromSpec).hom.app M)
    56	  haveI : IsIso sectionHom := by
    57	    dsimp only [sectionHom]
    58	    exact IsIso.comp_isIso' (fromSpecRestrictTopHom_isIso M hU) inferInstance
    59	  haveI : IsIso N.fromTildeΓ := isIso_fromTildeΓ_of_isQuasicoherent N
    60	  let eIndex : (ULift.{u} (Fin e) →₀ Γ(X, U)) ≃ₗ[Γ(X, U)] (Fin e → Γ(X, U)) :=
    61	    (Finsupp.linearEquivFunOnFinite Γ(X, U) Γ(X, U) (ULift.{u} (Fin e))).trans
    62	      (LinearEquiv.funCongrLeft Γ(X, U) Γ(X, U) Equiv.ulift.symm)
    63	  let eSections : (ULift.{u} (Fin e) →₀ Γ(X, U)) ≃ₗ[Γ(X, U)]
    64	      moduleSpecΓFunctor.obj N :=
    65	    eIndex.trans (E.trans (asIso sectionHom).toLinearEquiv)
    66	  let eSpec : N ≅
    67	      SheafOfModules.free (R := (Spec Γ(X, U)).ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin e)) :=
    68	    qcoh_iso_tilde_sections N ≪≫
    69	      (tilde.functor Γ(X, U)).mapIso eSections.toModuleIso.symm ≪≫
    70	      tildeFinsupp (ULift.{u} (Fin e))
    71	  have hcomp : hU.isoSpec.hom ≫ hU.fromSpec = U.ι := by
    72	    rw [← hU.isoSpec_inv_ι, Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc]
    73	  exact ⟨
    74	    ((pullbackCongr hcomp).symm.app M) ≪≫
    75	      ((pullbackComp hU.isoSpec.hom hU.fromSpec).app M).symm ≪≫
    76	      (pullback hU.isoSpec.hom).mapIso eSpec ≪≫
    77	      pullbackFreeIso hU.isoSpec.hom (ULift.{u} (Fin e))⟩

    79	/-- The entry-ideal stratum is locally free of its prescribed rank.  This is
    80	the locally-free strengthening of `coherentSheafFlat_stratum`. -/
    81	theorem stratum_isLocallyFreeOfRank
    82	    (M : X.Modules) [M.IsQuasicoherent] {e : ℕ} (hcov : ChartsCover M e) :
    83	    SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
    84	      ((pullback (stratumι M e hcov)).obj M) e := by
    85	  let N := (pullback (stratumι M e hcov)).obj M
    86	  haveI : N.IsQuasicoherent :=
    87	    pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom (stratumι M e hcov) M inferInstance
    88	  let I := {V : X.affineOpens // IsPresentationChart M e V}
    89	  let W : I → (stratum M e hcov).Opens := fun j =>
    90	    stratumι M e hcov ⁻¹ᵁ j.1.1
    91	  refine ⟨I, W, ?_, fun j => ?_⟩
    92	  · rw [eq_top_iff]
    93	    intro z _
    94	    obtain ⟨V, hzV, hchart⟩ := hcov ((stratumι M e hcov).base z)
    95	    exact TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨⟨V, hchart⟩, hzV⟩
    96	  · obtain ⟨mm, ⟨P⟩⟩ := j.2
    97	    have hW : IsAffineOpen (W j) :=
    98	      j.1.2.preimage (stratumι M e hcov)
    99	    obtain ⟨P', hP'⟩ := exists_matrixPresentation_pullback_sections
   100	      (stratumι M e hcov) M j.1.2 hW le_rfl P
   101	    have h0 : P'.relMatrix = 0 := by
   102	      rw [hP']
   103	      ext a b
   104	      simp only [Matrix.map_apply, Matrix.zero_apply]
   105	      have hmem : ((stratumι M e hcov).app j.1.1).hom (P.relMatrix a b) = 0 := by
   106	        have hker : P.relMatrix a b ∈
   107	            RingHom.ker (((strataData M e hcov).subschemeι.app j.1.1).hom) := by
   108	          rw [Scheme.IdealSheafData.ker_subschemeι_app]
   109	          change P.relMatrix a b ∈ strataIdeal M e j.1
   110	          rw [strataIdeal_eq_entryIdeal M P]
   111	          exact P.relMatrix_mem_entryIdeal a b
   112	        exact RingHom.mem_ker.mp hker
   113	      change ((stratumι M e hcov).appLE j.1.1 (W j) le_rfl).hom
   114	          (P.relMatrix a b) = 0
   115	      have happ : ((stratumι M e hcov).appLE j.1.1 (W j) le_rfl).hom
   116	          (P.relMatrix a b) =
   117	          ((stratum M e hcov).presheaf.map (homOfLE le_rfl).op).hom
   118	            (((stratumι M e hcov).app j.1.1).hom (P.relMatrix a b)) := rfl
   119	      rw [happ, hmem, map_zero]
   120	    exact pullback_isFreeOfRank_of_sectionsEquiv N hW e (P'.projEquiv h0)

   122	/-- Rank-indexed local freeness transports along an isomorphism of module
   123	sheaves, in arbitrary universe. -/
   124	theorem isLocallyFreeOfRank_of_iso_general {M N : X.Modules} (E : M ≅ N)
   125	    {e : ℕ} (hN : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank N e) :
   126	    SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank M e := by
   127	  obtain ⟨I, U, hU, hfree⟩ := hN
   128	  exact ⟨I, U, hU, fun i => ⟨(pullback (U i).ι).mapIso E ≪≫ (hfree i).some⟩⟩
   129	
   130	/-- The canonical locally closed rank stratum carries a locally free module
   131	of exactly the indexed rank. -/
   132	theorem rankStratum_isLocallyFreeOfRank {S : Scheme.{u}}
   133	    (F : S.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (e : ℕ) :
   134	    SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
   135	      ((pullback (rankStratumι F e)).obj F) e := by
   136	  let G := (pullback (chartLocus F e).ι).obj F
   137	  haveI : G.IsQuasicoherent :=
   138	    pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom (chartLocus F e).ι F inferInstance
   139	  let hcov : ChartsCover G e := chartsCover_chartLocus F e
   140	  have hfree := stratum_isLocallyFreeOfRank G hcov
   141	  let E : (pullback (rankStratumι F e)).obj F ≅
   142	      (pullback (stratumι G e hcov)).obj G :=
   143	    ((pullbackComp (stratumι G e hcov) (chartLocus F e).ι).app F).symm
   144	  exact isLocallyFreeOfRank_of_iso_general E hfree

   146	/-- The locally closed locus on which a module has rank one. -/
   147	noncomputable abbrev lineBundleLocus {S : Scheme.{u}} (F : S.Modules)
   148	    [F.IsQuasicoherent] : Scheme.{u} :=
   149	  rankStratum F 1

   151	/-- The immersion of the rank-one locus into its base. -/
   152	noncomputable abbrev lineBundleLocusι {S : Scheme.{u}} (F : S.Modules)
   153	    [F.IsQuasicoherent] : lineBundleLocus F ⟶ S :=

   159	/-- The support of the rank-one locus is exactly the point-rank-one set. -/
   160	theorem mem_range_lineBundleLocusι_iff {S : Scheme.{u}}
   161	    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (F : S.Modules) [F.IsFinitePresentation] (s : S) :
   162	    s ∈ Set.range (lineBundleLocusι F).base ↔ pointRank S F s = 1 :=

   165	/-- On the rank-one locus the pulled-back module is an invertible sheaf. -/
   166	theorem lineBundleLocus_isLocallyTrivial {S : Scheme.{u}}
   167	    (F : S.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
   168	    LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial
   169	      ((pullback (lineBundleLocusι F)).obj F) := by
   170	  obtain ⟨I, U, hU, hfree⟩ := rankStratum_isLocallyFreeOfRank F 1
   171	  apply LineBundle.isLocallyTrivial_of_pointwise_free_one
   172	  intro x
   173	  have hx : x ∈ ⨆ i, U i := by rw [hU]; trivial
   174	  obtain ⟨i, hxi⟩ := TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_iSup.mp hx
   175	  exact ⟨U i, hxi, hfree i⟩

   177	/-- A locally trivial line bundle is flat over its base.  This is the
   178	representation-facing form of the chart-local flatness recorded by
   179	`LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial`: on a trivialising affine chart its section
   180	module is linearly equivalent to the coordinate ring. -/
   181	theorem coherentSheafFlat_id_of_isLocallyTrivial {S : Scheme.{u}}
   182	    {F : S.Modules} (hF : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial F) :
   183	    Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 S) F := by
   184	  haveI : F.IsFinitePresentation := hF.isFinitePresentation
   185	  obtain ⟨I, U, hUaff, hUtop, hUiso⟩ := hF.exists_trivializing_cover
   186	  apply coherentSheafFlat_id_of_charts F U hUaff
   187	  · intro s
   188	    have hs : s ∈ iSup U := by rw [hUtop]; trivial
   189	    exact TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_iSup.mp hs
   190	  · intro i
   191	    let eRes : F.restrict (U i).ι ≅
   192	        (restrictFunctor (U i).ι).obj
   193	          (SheafOfModules.unit S.ringCatSheaf) :=
   194	      (hUiso i).some ≪≫
   195	        ((restrictFunctorIsoPullback (U i).ι).app
   196	          (SheafOfModules.unit S.ringCatSheaf) ≪≫ pullbackUnitIso (U i).ι).symm
   197	    let eΓ : Γ(F, U i) ≃ₗ[Γ(S, U i)] Γ(S, U i) :=
   198	      sectionLinearEquivOfRestrictIso (U i) eRes
   199	    exact Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv (M := Γ(S, U i)) eΓ

   201	/-- Every fibre of a locally trivial line bundle has dimension one. -/
   202	theorem pointRank_eq_one_of_isLocallyTrivial {S : Scheme.{u}}
   203	    {F : S.Modules} [F.IsQuasicoherent]
   204	    (hF : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial F) (s : S) :
   205	    pointRank S F s = 1 := by
   206	  obtain ⟨U, hsU, hUaff, ⟨eU⟩⟩ := hF s
   207	  let V : S.affineOpens := ⟨U, hUaff⟩
   208	  have hsV : s ∈ V.1 := hsU
   209	  rw [pointRank_eq_chartFiberRank F (V := V) s hsV]
   210	  let p : PrimeSpectrum Γ(S, U) := hUaff.primeIdealOf ⟨s, hsU⟩
   211	  haveI : Nontrivial Γ(S, U) := PrimeSpectrum.nontrivial p
   212	  change p.asIdeal.fiberRank Γ(F, U) = 1
   213	  let eRes : F.restrict U.ι ≅
   214	      (restrictFunctor U.ι).obj (SheafOfModules.unit S.ringCatSheaf) :=
   215	    eU ≪≫ ((restrictFunctorIsoPullback U.ι).app
   216	      (SheafOfModules.unit S.ringCatSheaf) ≪≫ pullbackUnitIso U.ι).symm
   217	  let eΓ : Γ(F, U) ≃ₗ[Γ(S, U)] Γ(S, U) :=
   218	    sectionLinearEquivOfRestrictIso U eRes
   219	  rw [Ideal.fiberRank_congr _ eΓ]
   220	  exact (Ideal.finrank_fiber_eq_rankAtStalk _).trans
   221	    (congrFun (Module.rankAtStalk_self (R := Γ(S, U))) p)

   226	theorem existsUnique_factor_lineBundleLocus {S : Scheme.{u}}

   237	theorem existsUnique_factor_lineBundleLocus_of_isLocallyTrivial

   255	variable {S X : Scheme.{u}} {π : X ⟶ S} {T : Over S}
   256	
   257	/-- The evaluation on `X_T` attached to a Grassmannian quotient of `π_* L`.
   258	
   259	The base-change map sends `T^*(π_*L)` to `pr_{T*}(pr_X^*L)`.  Precomposing
   260	with the kernel inclusion of the Grassmannian quotient and transposing along
   261	`pr_T^* ⊣ pr_{T*}` gives the displayed map.  Its kernel is not itself the
   262	divisor ideal: the divisor candidate is obtained from its cokernel below. -/
   263	noncomputable def kernelEvaluation (L : X.Modules) {d : ℕ}
   264	    (q : LocallyFreeQuotient ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) d T) :
   265	    (Modules.pullback (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (kernel q.q) ⟶
   266	      (Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L :=
   267	  ((Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
   268	    (pullback.snd π T.hom)).homEquiv _ _).symm
   269	    (kernel.ι q.q ≫
   270	      pushforwardBaseChangeMap π T.hom (pullback.snd π T.hom)
   271	        (pullback.fst π T.hom) pullback.condition L)
   272	
   273	/-- The quotient on `X_T` reconstructed from a Grassmannian quotient: take the
   274	cokernel of `kernelEvaluation`.  The later D3 locus is where this quotient is
   275	a divisor quotient and its kernel is invertible. -/
   276	noncomputable def candidateQuotient (L : X.Modules) {d : ℕ}
   277	    (q : LocallyFreeQuotient ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) d T) :
   278	    (Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L ⟶
   279	      cokernel (kernelEvaluation L q) :=
   280	  cokernel.π (kernelEvaluation L q)
   281	
   282	/-- The reconstructed Grassmannian quotient is epimorphic by construction. -/
   283	theorem candidateQuotient_epi (L : X.Modules) {d : ℕ}
   284	    (q : LocallyFreeQuotient ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) d T) :
   285	    Epi (candidateQuotient L q) := by
   286	  dsimp only [candidateQuotient]
   287	  infer_instance
   288	
   289	/-- The candidate twisted divisor ideal attached to a Grassmannian quotient. -/
   290	noncomputable def candidateIdeal (L : X.Modules) {d : ℕ}
   291	    (q : LocallyFreeQuotient ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) d T) :
   292	    (pullback π T.hom).Modules :=
   293	  kernel (candidateQuotient L q)
   294

    10	/-!
    11	# Pushing a divisor family down to the base, flatly
    12	
    13	Campaign milestone **D3'** (`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md:305`) asks
    14	for the locus over which a Grassmannian `T`-point arises from a degree-`d`
    15	`DivFamily` to be locally closed *universally*, by extending
    16	`AlgebraicGeometry.flatLocusStratification_universal`
    17	(`Picard/FlatteningStratificationUniversal.lean`) "to the family `C × G → G`".
    18	
    19	This file supplies the object that extension has to be about, and records why the
    20	extension has to be phrased this way rather than by relativising the machine.
    21	
    22	## The shape of the reduction, and why it is forced
    23	
    24	`flatLocusStratification_universal` is stated for a module **on the base**,
    25	`F : S.Modules`, with `π = 𝟙 S`. That is not an accident of its proof that a
    26	later session can relax: the whole stratification machine is built on
    27	`Scheme.Modules.pointRank : (X : Scheme) → X.Modules → ↥X → ℕ`, which takes a
    28	module on *one* scheme and a point of *that* scheme. There is no relative
    29	`pointRank` over a morphism, and `chartLocus`, `rankStratum`,
    30	`isOpen_pointRank_pullback_eq` and `existsUnique_factor_rankStratum` all inherit
    31	that shape. So a general-`π` universal property cannot be obtained by adding a
    32	`π` to those statements; the family has to be *moved to the base* first.
    33	
    34	For a divisor family that move is available, and cheaply, because a relative
    35	effective divisor is finite over the base — where a general proper family is not.
    36	Concretely: `Scheme.Modules.HasProperSupport` is by definition
    37	`IsProper (schematicSupportι F ≫ f)` (`Picard/QuotScheme.lean`), and
    38	`DivFamily.properSupport` is exactly that datum for `f = pullback.snd π T.hom`.
    39	A proper *quasi-finite* morphism is finite (`IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite`),
    40	hence affine, and `Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat` transfers along an affine
    41	pushforward. Since `O_D` is the pushforward of its own restriction to the support
    42	(`schematicSupportDescentIso`), the family's flatness over `T` becomes flatness of
    43	`q_* O_D` over `T` *itself* — the `n = 0` shape the universal property consumes.
    44	
    45	## What is proved here, and what is assumed
    46	
    47	* `Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.of_pushforward_of_isAffineHom` — the **converse** of
    48	  `Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.pushforward_of_isAffineHom`
    49	  (`Picard/RigidPushforwardTransfer.lean`), which did not exist. Both directions
    50	  are the same chart computation read in opposite directions; the content is that
    51	  the two `Γ(T, U)`-module structures on `Γ(F, π ⁻¹ᵁ V)` agree, which is
    52	  `Scheme.Hom.appLE_comp_appLE`.
    53	
    54	* `Scheme.DivFamily.coherentSheafFlat_id_pushforward` — for a divisor family whose
    55	  divisor is quasi-finite over the base, `q_* O_D` is flat over `T` in the
    56	  `CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 T.left)` sense.
    57	
    58	**The quasi-finiteness is a hypothesis, not a theorem, and this file does not
    59	pretend otherwise.** `LocallyQuasiFinite (schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom)`
    60	says the divisor `D ⊆ X_T` has finite fibres over `T`. Mathematically it is
    61	relative-dimension-1 content: on the curve fibre `C_t`, `D_t` is the zero scheme
    62	of a regular section of an invertible ideal, hence `0`-dimensional. It has no
    63	producer in this project, and `LocallyQuasiFinite` occurs nowhere else in
    64	`Picard/`. It is stated as an instance binder so that a later producer discharges
    65	every consumer at once.
    66	
    67	Worth recording for whoever prices the next step: this hypothesis is *cleaner*
    68	than the one it replaces. `Picard/DivDegree.lean` gates its clopen degree
    69	decomposition on `HasLocallyConstantDivDeg`, a `Prop`-class carrying local
    70	constancy of `fiberDeg` as an assumption and also without a producer. With
    71	quasi-finiteness instead, local constancy is downstream of a stratification
    72	theorem rather than assumed beside it — the same missing geometry, but bought
    73	once and in a form the machine can use.
    74	
    75	## What remains for D3'
    76	
    77	`flatLocusStratification_universal` has exactly **two** binders:
    78	`[IsNoetherian S]` and `[F.IsFinitePresentation]`. `IsQuasicoherent` is a mathlib
    79	instance *from* finite presentation, so it is not a separate requirement;
    80	`DivFamily.isQuasicoherent_pushforward` below is kept because it is the cheap half
    81	and is wanted in its own right, not because `:876` asks for it.
    82	
    83	Finite presentation of `q_* O_D` is `DivFamily.isFinitePresentation_pushforward`,
    84	proved here. `isFinitePresentation_of_finite_sections`
    85	(`Picard/RigidPushforwardTransfer.lean`) reduces it to `Module.Finite Γ(T,V)
    86	Γ(q_* O_D, V)` on affine `V`, and that tower is:
    87	
    88	* `Module.Finite Γ(T,V) Γ(D,W)` for `W := (i ≫ q) ⁻¹ᵁ V`, from
    89	  `IsFinite.finite_app` — this is where the finiteness of the support map is spent,
    90	  and it is exactly what quasi-finiteness bought;
    91	* `Module.Finite Γ(D,W) Γ(N,W)` from `finite_sections_preimage_of_isAffineHom`
    92	  together with `isFinitePresentation_pullback_schematicSupportι`;
    93	* the two compose by `Module.Finite.trans`, and the result transports back across
    94	  `schematicSupportDescentIso` because `Γ(q_* F, V) = Γ(F, q ⁻¹ᵁ V)` and
    95	  `Γ(i_* N, q ⁻¹ᵁ V) = Γ(N, (i ≫ q) ⁻¹ᵁ V)` are both `rfl`, and the native
    96	  `Γ(T,V)`-action on `Γ(q_* F, V)` *is* `compHom` along `q.app V`, also `rfl`. The
    97	  semilinearity is `Scheme.Modules.Hom.app_smul`.
    98	
    99	## What remains for D3'
   100	
   101	Two things, and neither is supplied here.
   102	
   103	**A stated bridge, not a free fit.** `:876` stratifies a module on the base and
   104	quantifies its universal property over test morphisms `φ : T' ⟶ S`; its antecedent
   105	asks for `CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 T') ((Modules.pullback φ).obj F)`. What
   106	`coherentSheafFlat_id_pushforward` gives is the `φ = 𝟙` case *before* the identity
   107	pullback is reduced, so feeding it needs
   108	`(Scheme.Modules.pullbackId T.left).app _` through `coherentSheafFlat_of_iso` —
   109	one line, but a line, and it discharges the `φ = 𝟙` **instance** rather than the
   110	antecedent as a family. Whether that instance is what D3' needs is not settled in
   111	this file and should be settled before D3' is priced as "inputs done".
   112	
   113	**The `∃!` statement about the Grassmannian locus itself**, which is D3' proper.
   114	
   115	Nothing in this file closes D3'.
   116	
   117	## Honest status of every antecedent
   118	
   119	`Scheme.DivFamily` itself has **no producer anywhere in this project** — 135
   120	mention sites, all consumers (measured 2026-07-29, inbox `I-0957`). So the
   121	theorems here, like the rest of Cluster D', are true statements about a carrier
   122	nobody has yet inhabited; that is a property of the cluster, not of this file, and
   123	it is recorded rather than hidden. The `LocallyQuasiFinite` binder has no producer
   124	either, and is *not* derivable from `DivFamily`'s other fields (kernel-checked),
   125	so it is genuine content and not a restatement of `properSupport`.
   126	-/
   127	
   128	universe u
   129	
   130	open CategoryTheory Limits
   131	
   132	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
   133	
   134	/-- **Coherent-sheaf flatness descends along an affine pushforward** — the
   135	converse of `Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.pushforward_of_isAffineHom`.
   136	
   137	For affine `π : X ⟶ Y` over `p : Y ⟶ T`, flatness of `π_* F` over `T` gives
   138	flatness of `F` over `T` along the composite. Read on an affine `V ⊆ Y`: the
   139	sections of `π_* F` over `V` *are* `Γ(F, π ⁻¹ᵁ V)` definitionally, with `π ⁻¹ᵁ V`
   140	affine because `π` is, and the two `Γ(T, U)`-module structures agree because
   141	`(π ≫ p).appLE = p.appLE ≫ π.appLE`.
   142	
   143	Flatness on the preimage charts `π ⁻¹ᵁ V` of an affine cover of `Y` is what the
   144	hypothesis gives directly; `flat_section_of_affine_cover` globalises it to every
   145	affine pair of `X`, which is where quasi-coherence of `F` is used. -/
   146	theorem Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.of_pushforward_of_isAffineHom
   147	    {X Y T : Scheme.{u}} (π : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffineHom π] (p : Y ⟶ T)
   148	    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
   149	    (h : Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat p ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward π).obj F)) :
   150	    Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat (π ≫ p) F := by

600	  refine representable_of_openCover (Scheme.Grassmannian V d)
   601	    (isZariskiSheaf V d) U hU (fun i => ?_)
   602	  obtain ⟨e⟩ := hloc i
   603	  exact representable_restrict (U i) e hd hdr
   604	
   605	/-! ## §7. The universal quotient on the chosen representing scheme -/
   606	
   607	/-- A chosen representing scheme for the relative Grassmannian.  This makes
   608	the existential output of `representable` available to constructions, such as
   609	the universal evaluation cokernel used in the divisor locus. -/
   610	noncomputable def representingScheme {V : S.Modules} {r d : ℕ}
   611	    (hV : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank V r)
   612	    (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdr : d ≤ r) : Over S :=
   613	  Classical.choose (representable hV hd hdr)
   614	
   615	/-- The chosen representation carried by `representingScheme`. -/
   616	noncomputable def representation {V : S.Modules} {r d : ℕ}
   617	    (hV : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank V r)
   618	    (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdr : d ≤ r) :
   619	    (Scheme.Grassmannian V d).RepresentableBy
   620	      (representingScheme hV hd hdr) :=
   621	  Classical.choice (Classical.choose_spec (representable hV hd hdr))
   622	
   623	/-- The universal Grassmannian class: the image of the identity of the chosen
   624	representing scheme under its `RepresentableBy` equivalence. -/
   625	noncomputable def universalClass {V : S.Modules} {r d : ℕ}
   626	    (hV : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank V r)
   627	    (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdr : d ≤ r) :
   628	    (Scheme.Grassmannian V d).obj
   629	      (Opposite.op (representingScheme hV hd hdr)) :=
   630	  (representation hV hd hdr).homEquiv (𝟙 _)
   631	
   632	/-- A quotient representative of the universal Grassmannian class.  Choosing
   633	the representative exposes its sheaf and quotient map to the D3 construction;
   634	all moduli statements remain at the quotient-class level. -/
   635	noncomputable def universalQuotient {V : S.Modules} {r d : ℕ}
   636	    (hV : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank V r)
   637	    (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdr : d ≤ r) :
   638	    LocallyFreeQuotient V d (representingScheme hV hd hdr) :=
   639	  Quotient.out (universalClass hV hd hdr)
   640	
   641	/-- The chosen universal quotient represents the universal class. -/
   642	theorem mk_universalQuotient {V : S.Modules} {r d : ℕ}
   643	    (hV : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank V r)
   644	    (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdr : d ≤ r) :
   645	    Quotient.mk _ (universalQuotient hV hd hdr) =
   646	      universalClass hV hd hdr :=
   647	  Quotient.out_eq _
   648	
   649	/-- Every point of the chosen representing scheme classifies the pullback of
   650	the universal quotient.  This is the representation-facing universal-family
   651	identity needed before forming a sheaf on `X ×_S Gr(V,d)`. -/
   652	theorem homEquiv_eq_pullback_universalQuotient
   653	    {V : S.Modules} {r d : ℕ}
   654	    (hV : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank V r)
   655	    (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdr : d ≤ r)
   656	    {T : Over S} (f : T ⟶ representingScheme hV hd hdr) :
   657	    (representation hV hd hdr).homEquiv f =
   658	      Quotient.mk _ (LocallyFreeQuotient.pullbackAlong f
   659	        (universalQuotient hV hd hdr)) := by
   660	  calc
   661	    (representation hV hd hdr).homEquiv f =
   662	        (Scheme.Grassmannian V d).map f.op
   663	          ((representation hV hd hdr).homEquiv (𝟙 _)) := by
   664	      rw [← (representation hV hd hdr).homEquiv_comp f (𝟙 _),
   665	        Category.comp_id]
   666	    _ = (Scheme.Grassmannian V d).map f.op
   667	          (Quotient.mk _ (universalQuotient hV hd hdr)) := by
   668	      exact congrArg ((Scheme.Grassmannian V d).map f.op)
   669	        (mk_universalQuotient hV hd hdr).symm
   670	    _ = Quotient.mk _ (LocallyFreeQuotient.pullbackAlong f
   671	          (universalQuotient hV hd hdr)) := rfl
   672	
   673	end Grassmannian
   674	
   675	end Scheme
   676	
   677	end AlgebraicGeometry

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivGrassmannianClass
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivLocallyClosed
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# The universal Grassmannian candidate for a divisor
    11	
    12	This file connects the D2 divisor-to-Grassmannian class to the D3
    13	curve-side candidate quotient.  It is kept downstream of both constructions
    14	so changes to this bridge do not force the large D2 development to recompile.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	set_option autoImplicit false
    18	
    19	universe u
    20	
    21	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory
    22	
    23	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    24	
    25	namespace Scheme
    26	
    27	namespace DivFamily
    28	
    29	variable {S X : Scheme.{u}} {π : X ⟶ S} {T : Over S}
    30	
    31	/-- The reconstructed Grassmannian evaluation kills the relations of an
    32	actual divisor family.  The proof is the adjunction transpose of
    33	`kernel.ι (grassmannianEval L x) ≫ grassmannianEval L x = 0`; it uses no
    34	additional hypothesis beyond the data already needed to form that quotient. -/
    35	theorem grassmannianKernelEvaluation_comp_twistQuotientMap
    36	    (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) [IsLocallyNoetherian S] {d : ℕ}
    37	    (hEpi : Epi (x.grassmannianEval L))
    38	    (hLocFree : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
    39	      ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L)) d) :
    40	    LocallyFreeQuotient.kernelEvaluation L
    41	        (x.grassmannianQuotient L hEpi hLocFree) ≫
    42	      x.twistQuotientMap L = 0 := by
    43	  let q := x.grassmannianQuotient L hEpi hLocFree
    44	  change LocallyFreeQuotient.kernelEvaluation L q ≫
    45	    x.twistQuotientMap L = 0
    46	  apply ((Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
    47	    (pullback.snd π T.hom)).homEquiv _ _).injective
    48	  rw [Adjunction.homEquiv_naturality_right]
    49	  simp only [LocallyFreeQuotient.kernelEvaluation, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
    50	  change (kernel.ι q.q ≫
    51	      pushforwardBaseChangeMap π T.hom (pullback.snd π T.hom)
    52	        (pullback.fst π T.hom) pullback.condition L) ≫
    53	      (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).map
    54	        (x.twistQuotientMap L) = _
    55	  rw [Category.assoc]
    56	  change kernel.ι q.q ≫ q.q = _
    57	  rw [kernel.condition, Adjunction.homAddEquiv_zero]
    58	  rfl
    59	
    60	/-- The canonical comparison from the Grassmannian candidate cokernel to the
    61	twisted sheaf of an actual divisor family. -/
    62	noncomputable def grassmannianCandidateToTwist
    63	    (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) [IsLocallyNoetherian S] {d : ℕ}
    64	    (hEpi : Epi (x.grassmannianEval L))
    65	    (hLocFree : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
    66	      ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L)) d) :
    67	    cokernel (LocallyFreeQuotient.kernelEvaluation L
    68	      (x.grassmannianQuotient L hEpi hLocFree)) ⟶ x.twist L :=
    69	  cokernel.desc _ (x.twistQuotientMap L)
    70	    (grassmannianKernelEvaluation_comp_twistQuotientMap
    71	      L x hEpi hLocFree)
    72	
    73	/-- The candidate quotient followed by its comparison is the original
    74	twisted divisor quotient. -/
    75	theorem grassmannianCandidateQuotient_comp_candidateToTwist
    76	    (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) [IsLocallyNoetherian S] {d : ℕ}
    77	    (hEpi : Epi (x.grassmannianEval L))
    78	    (hLocFree : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
    79	      ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L)) d) :
    80	    LocallyFreeQuotient.candidateQuotient L
    81	        (x.grassmannianQuotient L hEpi hLocFree) ≫
    82	      grassmannianCandidateToTwist L x hEpi hLocFree =
    83	        x.twistQuotientMap L :=
    84	  cokernel.π_desc _ _ _
    85	
    86	end DivFamily
    87	
    88	namespace Grassmannian
    89	
    90	variable {S X : Scheme.{0}} {π : X ⟶ S} [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    91	
    92	/-- The curve-side evaluation map attached to the universal quotient on the
    93	chosen scheme representing `Grassmannian (π_* L) d`. -/
    94	noncomputable def universalKernelEvaluation (L : X.Modules) {r d : ℕ}
    95	    (hV : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
    96	      ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) r)
    97	    (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdr : d ≤ r) :=
    98	  LocallyFreeQuotient.kernelEvaluation L
    99	    (universalQuotient hV hd hdr)
   100	
   101	/-- The universal candidate quotient on
   102	`X ×_S representingScheme (Grassmannian (π_*L) d)`. -/
   103	noncomputable def universalCandidateQuotient (L : X.Modules) {r d : ℕ}
   104	    (hV : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
   105	      ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) r)
   106	    (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdr : d ≤ r) :=
   107	  LocallyFreeQuotient.candidateQuotient L
   108	    (universalQuotient hV hd hdr)
   109	
   110	/-- The kernel of the universal candidate quotient.  This is the actual
   111	curve-side module whose invertible locus D3 must carve out; the kernel of the
   112	Grassmannian quotient itself lives on the base and has the wrong rank.  Its
   113	ordinary `lineBundleLocus` lies in the total space `X_G`; D3 must still descend
   114	the whole-fibre condition to a locus in the Grassmannian base `G`. -/
   115	noncomputable def universalCandidateIdeal (L : X.Modules) {r d : ℕ}
   116	    (hV : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
   117	      ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) r)
   118	    (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdr : d ≤ r) :=
   119	  LocallyFreeQuotient.candidateIdeal L
   120	    (universalQuotient hV hd hdr)
   121	
   122	/-- The universal candidate quotient is epimorphic by its cokernel
   123	construction. -/
   124	theorem universalCandidateQuotient_epi (L : X.Modules) {r d : ℕ}
   125	    (hV : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
   126	      ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) r)
   127	    (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdr : d ≤ r) :
   128	    Epi (universalCandidateQuotient L hV hd hdr) :=
   129	  LocallyFreeQuotient.candidateQuotient_epi L
   130	    (universalQuotient hV hd hdr)
   131	
   132	end Grassmannian
   133	
   134	end Scheme
   135	
   136	end AlgebraicGeometry

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FiniteMapProjectiveGluing
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.ProjectiveCoordinateRelativeChart
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# The projective immersion attached to a finite two-chart map
    11	
    12	The two distinguished homogeneous coordinates cut out target charts whose
    13	inverse images are exactly the two pulled-back Laurent charts.  On each chart,
    14	the global relative coordinate morphism is the closed immersion supplied by
    15	the algebra-generating coordinate family.  Target-locality then makes the
    16	global morphism an immersion.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	set_option autoImplicit false
    20	
    21	noncomputable section
    22	
    23	universe u
    24	
    25	open CategoryTheory Limits MvPolynomial HomogeneousLocalization
    26	  TopologicalSpace AlgebraicGeometry
    27	
    28	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic
    29	namespace LaurentChartData.FiniteMapGenerators
    30	
    31	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
    32	variable {Y C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
    33	variable {D : LaurentChartData Y} {pi : C ⟶ Y}
    34	variable (G : D.FiniteMapGenerators pi)
    35	
    36	/-- The coordinate normalized to one on the first source chart. -/
    37	abbrev firstIndex : G.ProjectiveIndex :=
    38	  Sum.inl ⟨0, Nat.zero_lt_succ G.d⟩
    39	
    40	/-- The coordinate normalized to one on the second source chart. -/
    41	abbrev secondIndex : G.ProjectiveIndex :=
    42	  Sum.inl ⟨G.d, Nat.lt_succ_self G.d⟩
    43	
    44	/-- The target chart selected by the first distinguished coordinate. -/
    45	def targetOpen0 : (ℙ(G.ProjectiveIndex; Spec (.of k))).Opens :=
    46	  ProjectiveSpace.toProjInt G.ProjectiveIndex (Spec (.of k)) ⁻¹ᵁ
    47	    Proj.basicOpen
    48	      (homogeneousSubmodule G.ProjectiveIndex (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X G.firstIndex)
    49	
    50	/-- The target chart selected by the second distinguished coordinate. -/
    51	def targetOpen1 : (ℙ(G.ProjectiveIndex; Spec (.of k))).Opens :=
    52	  ProjectiveSpace.toProjInt G.ProjectiveIndex (Spec (.of k)) ⁻¹ᵁ
    53	    Proj.basicOpen
    54	      (homogeneousSubmodule G.ProjectiveIndex (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X G.secondIndex)
    55	
    56	/-- The first target open is the corresponding relative affine chart. -/
    57	def targetOpen0IsoAffineChartAt :
    58	    G.targetOpen0.toScheme ≅
    59	      ProjectiveSpace.affineChartAt G.ProjectiveIndex G.firstIndex (Spec (.of k)) := by
    60	  apply IsOpenImmersion.isoOfRangeEq G.targetOpen0.ι
    61	    (ProjectiveSpace.affineChartAt.incl
    62	      G.ProjectiveIndex G.firstIndex (Spec (.of k)))
    63	  rw [Scheme.Opens.range_ι, ← Scheme.Hom.coe_opensRange,
    64	    ProjectiveSpace.affineChartAt.opensRange_incl, targetOpen0]
    65	
    66	/-- The second target open is the corresponding relative affine chart. -/
    67	def targetOpen1IsoAffineChartAt :
    68	    G.targetOpen1.toScheme ≅
    69	      ProjectiveSpace.affineChartAt G.ProjectiveIndex G.secondIndex (Spec (.of k)) := by
    70	  apply IsOpenImmersion.isoOfRangeEq G.targetOpen1.ι
    71	    (ProjectiveSpace.affineChartAt.incl
    72	      G.ProjectiveIndex G.secondIndex (Spec (.of k)))
    73	  rw [Scheme.Opens.range_ι, ← Scheme.Hom.coe_opensRange,
    74	    ProjectiveSpace.affineChartAt.opensRange_incl, targetOpen1]
    75

    10	/-!
    11	# Global immersion of the Plucker morphism
    12	
    13	The inverse image of the standard projective open indexed by `I` is exactly
    14	the range of the `I`-th affine Grassmannian chart. On this open, the global
    15	Plucker morphism is therefore identified with the local immersion proved in
    16	`GrassmannianPluckerImmersion`. Since the standard projective opens cover the
    17	target, the global Plucker morphism is an immersion.
    18	-/

    20	open CategoryTheory Limits MvPolynomial
    21	
    22	noncomputable section
    23	
    24	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    25	namespace Grassmannian

    27	/-- The range of a Grassmannian chart localization is the principal open cut
    28	out by its transition minor. -/
    29	theorem chartIncl_opensRange (d r : ℕ) (I J : PluckerIndex d r) :
    30	    (chartIncl d r I.1 J.1 I.2 J.2).opensRange =
    31	      PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (minorDet d r I.1 J.1 I.2 J.2) := by
    32	  change (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
    33	    (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin d × {q : Fin r // q ∉ I.1}) ℤ)
    34	      (Localization.Away (minorDet d r I.1 J.1 I.2 J.2))))).opensRange = _
    35	  exact TopologicalSpace.Opens.ext
    36	    (PrimeSpectrum.localization_away_comap_range
    37	      (Localization.Away (minorDet d r I.1 J.1 I.2 J.2))
    38	      (minorDet d r I.1 J.1 I.2 J.2))
    39	
    40	/-- Inside one affine Grassmannian chart, the inverse image of another chart's
    41	range is the overlap localization. -/
    42	theorem glueChart_preimage_opensRange (d r : ℕ)
    43	    (I J : (theGlueData d r).J) :
    44	    (theGlueData d r).ι J ⁻¹ᵁ ((theGlueData d r).ι I).opensRange =
    45	      (chartIncl d r J.1 I.1 J.2 I.2).opensRange := by
    46	  have hp := IsPullback.of_isLimit ((theGlueData d r).vPullbackConeIsLimit J I)
    47	  change (theGlueData d r).ι J ⁻¹ᵁ ((theGlueData d r).ι I).opensRange =
    48	    ((theGlueData d r).f J I).opensRange
    49	  rw [← Scheme.Hom.opensRange_pullbackFst]
    50	  have hfst := hp.isoPullback_hom_fst
    51	  change hp.isoPullback.hom ≫
    52	      pullback.fst ((theGlueData d r).ι J) ((theGlueData d r).ι I) =
    53	    (theGlueData d r).f J I at hfst
    54	  have hrange :
    55	      (hp.isoPullback.hom ≫ pullback.fst ((theGlueData d r).ι J)
    56	        ((theGlueData d r).ι I)).opensRange =
    57	      (pullback.fst ((theGlueData d r).ι J)
    58	        ((theGlueData d r).ι I)).opensRange := by
    59	    rw [Scheme.Hom.opensRange_comp, Scheme.Hom.opensRange_of_isIso]
    60	    simp
    61	  rw [← hrange]
    62	  congr 1

   101	/-- The affine chart is canonically isomorphic to its open range in the glued

   103	def pluckerChartRangeIso (d r : ℕ) (I : (theGlueData d r).J) :
   104	    affineChart d r I.1 ≅ (((theGlueData d r).ι I).opensRange).toScheme := by
   105	  apply IsOpenImmersion.isoOfRangeEq
   106	    ((theGlueData d r).ι I) (((theGlueData d r).ι I).opensRange).ι

   110	/-- The absolute Plucker morphism is an immersion. -/
   111	theorem pluckerToProj_isImmersion (d r : ℕ) :
   112	    IsImmersion (pluckerToProj d r) := by
   113	  apply IsZariskiLocalAtTarget.of_iSup_eq_top
   114	    (P := @IsImmersion)
   115	    (fun I : PluckerIndex d r =>
   116	      Proj.basicOpen (homogeneousSubmodule (PluckerIndex d r) (ULift ℤ)) (X I))
   117	    (ProjTwist.iSup_basicOpen_X_eq_top (PluckerIndex d r))
   118	  intro I
   119	  let U := Proj.basicOpen
   120	    (homogeneousSubmodule (PluckerIndex d r) (ULift ℤ)) (X I)
   121	  let V := ((theGlueData d r).ι I).opensRange
   122	  let e : affineChart d r I.1 ≅ V.toScheme := pluckerChartRangeIso d r I
   123	  let g : V.toScheme ⟶ U.toScheme :=
   124	    (pluckerToProj d r).resLE U V (pluckerToProj_preimage_basicOpen d r I).ge
   125	  have he : e.hom ≫ V.ι = (theGlueData d r).ι I := by
   126	    exact IsOpenImmersion.isoOfRangeEq_hom_fac _ _ _
   127	  have hgfac : e.hom ≫ (g ≫ U.ι) = pluckerChart d r I := by
   128	    rw [Scheme.Hom.resLE_comp_ι]
   129	    rw [← Category.assoc, he, ι_pluckerToProj]
   130	  have hcomp : IsImmersion (e.hom ≫ (g ≫ U.ι)) := by
   131	    rw [hgfac]
   132	    exact pluckerChart_isImmersion d r I
   133	  haveI : IsImmersion (g ≫ U.ι) :=
   134	    (MorphismProperty.cancel_left_of_respectsIso
   135	      (@IsImmersion) e.hom (g ≫ U.ι)).mp hcomp
   136	  have hg : IsImmersion g := IsImmersion.of_comp g U.ι
   137	  rw [MorphismProperty.arrow_mk_iso_iff (P := @IsImmersion)
   138	    (AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.LaurentChartData.FiniteMapGenerators.restrictionIsoResLE
   139	      (pluckerToProj d r) U V (pluckerToProj_preimage_basicOpen d r I))]
